title: The AI investment cycle
deck: Capital is arriving before the cash flows. The question is not whether AI is real, but how much of the buildout can earn its cost of capital.
author: NEXUS Research
takeaway: The base case is a multi-year infrastructure cycle with near-term margin pressure. Value accrues first to scarce compute and later to distribution.

sections.title: The buildout is the story
sections.body: Hyperscaler capital expenditure is becoming the cleanest observable measure of conviction. Spending is broadening beyond training clusters into networking, power, and inference capacity. That broadening is healthy for the cycle, but it also raises the break-even threshold.

sections.title: Scarcity moves up the stack
sections.body: The leading constraint has migrated from model access to power, advanced packaging, and time-to-deploy. This makes the cycle less like a software launch and more like a semiconductor expansion with software-shaped demand.

sections.title: What would change our view
sections.body: We would become more constructive on durable software capture if inference prices stabilize while seat expansion continues. We would turn cautious if capex growth persists alongside falling utilization and shortening contract duration.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.summary: Agents create measurable labor leverage; utilization compounds into software margins.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.summary: Infrastructure earns through steady workload migration; returns normalize over time.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.summary: Overbuild meets commoditizing inference and the capex payback stretches out.
